# 05 · Critic Framework

Critics are independent reviewers with one mandate each. They run blind (fresh context, no author rationale, no prior-round history) and report only concrete, material deficiencies. See `gauntlet/PROTOCOL.md` for the loop, severity scale and convergence rule.

## Stages

- **G1** — Framework gauntlet: capability map, skill graph, contracts, hierarchy (whole framework)
- **G2** — SKILL.md gauntlet: per-skill description quality, technique currency, validation criteria
- **S1** — ADR review: evidence, alternatives, revisit conditions
- **S2** — Design & contract review: API/contract drafts, data layouts, threading model
- **S3** — Implementation review: code, tests, instrumentation
- **S4** — Validation & release review: benchmarks, scalability runs, certification readiness

## Critics

### K-ARCH · Engine Architecture Critic

Architectural completeness and subsystem boundaries: ownership overlaps, missing contracts, wrong layering, contracts that leak internals, hierarchy that does not match coupling.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2
- Scope: all, tier:orchestrator, research-evidence, subtree:api-lifecycle-migration, subtree:world-architect, developer-experience-docs
- Checks: every capability has exactly one owner and the owner is the right expertise; non-responsibilities point to the real owner; contracts are minimal, stable and layered; no hidden cyclic build dependencies; leads have real territory, not just coordination

### K-RENDER · Rendering Critic

Graphics architecture and currency of rendering techniques; GPU-driven, bindless, explicit-API assumptions; scalability from 2D mobile to path tracing.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: atmosphere-weather, deformation-skinning, gpu-performance, media-playback, ml-inference-runtime, platform-console, render-validation, subtree:gpu-platform-architect, subtree:render-architect, terrain, text-fonts, vegetation-foliage, visual-debugging-tools, voxel-worlds, water-ocean, world-editor-viewport, xr-runtime
- Checks: no draw-call-centric or DX11-era assumptions on capable tiers; CPU-batched submission on TBDR/lite3d follows RND.ARCH.submission-strategy; render graph owns sync and aliasing; technique maturity labels are honest; scale-down path exists for each feature

### K-SYSTEMS · Systems Critic

Concurrency, memory, scheduling, IO and low-level architecture.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: subtree:core-runtime-architect, subtree:resource-streaming-architect, observability-telemetry, crash-diagnostics, determinism-replay, hot-reload-iteration, rhi-core, gpu-memory-resources, render-graph-scheduling, audio-architect, network-transport, ml-inference-runtime, subtree:world-architect, subtree:gpu-platform-architect, runtime-scalability, media-playback
- Checks: no single-thread-first assumptions; explicit ownership and lifetimes; synchronization minimized and justified; async IO end to end; heterogeneous cores and NUMA considered

### K-SIM · Physics & Simulation Critic

Simulation domains: physics, destruction, fluids, cloth, crowds, large-scale simulation, determinism of simulation.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: character-movement, crowd-simulation, determinism-replay, gameplay-systems-toolkit, ik-procedural-animation, navigation-pathfinding, prediction-rollback, procedural-generation, simulation-validation, subtree:physics-architect, systems-simulation, vfx-particles, voxel-worlds, water-ocean
- Checks: stepping and sync with frame phases are explicit; determinism levels are declared; simulation LOD exists for large scales; build-vs-integrate evidence; fixed-step only; sub-rates declared; snapshot/resim participation and cost declared; C-SIGNIF tier-transition handlers declared

### K-NET · Networking Critic

Online and multiplayer architecture: models, replication, prediction, servers, security, online-service boundaries.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: animation-architect, animation-runtime, anti-cheat-integrity, audio-dsp-mixing, character-movement, cinematics-sequencer, crowd-simulation, destruction-fracture, determinism-replay, editor-architect, frame-orchestration, functional-automation-soak, gameplay-systems-toolkit, input-system, modding-ugc, narrative-dialogue, net-session, online-performance, online-services-liveops, packaging-release-patching, persistence-save, physics-2d, physics-architect, platform-server-host, platform-services, platform-web, rigid-body-dynamics, server-scaleout-persistence, simulation-validation, subtree:network-architect, vehicle-physics, voxel-worlds
- Checks: netcode model matches game type; authority and trust explicit; bandwidth and scale budgets; version compatibility; service boundaries clear

### K-TOOLS · Tools & Editor Critic

Production tooling and content workflows: editor, pipeline, collaboration, iteration speed.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: subtree:editor-architect, subtree:content-pipeline-architect, hot-reload-iteration, developer-experience-docs, ui-architect, terrain, procedural-generation, cinematics-sequencer, scripting-runtime, world-data-model, subtree:build-release-architect, owns-area:TOOL, kind:tool, api-lifecycle-migration
- Checks: tooling as thorough as runtime; undo/transactions universal; large teams can collaborate without lock contention; iteration time measured; pipeline deterministic and cached

### K-PLATFORM · Platform Critic

Hardware, operating systems, consoles, graphics APIs, packaging and platform requirements.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S4, S3
- Scope: subtree:platform-architect, rhi-core, subtree:build-release-architect, certification-compliance, async-io-storage, crash-diagnostics, rhi-d3d12, rhi-vulkan, rhi-metal, rhi-webgpu
- Checks: PAL is the only platform-specific layer; console, mobile and web constraints represented; certification requirements traced; packaging and patching per platform

### K-PERF · Performance Critic

Scalability bottlenecks: serialization points, excess synchronization, cache inefficiency, GPU stalls, bandwidth, poor asymptotics.

- Stages: G1, G2, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: all, subtree:performance-architect, subtree:world-architect, runtime-scalability
- Checks: budgets exist for each subsystem; benchmarks include realistic workloads; no hidden global sync points; asymptotics stated for world-scale data

### K-PROD · Production Critic

Could a real team ship games with this: workflows, content scale, team scale, schedules, live operations.

- Stages: G1, G2, S4
- Scope: all, tier:orchestrator, developer-experience-docs, subtree:build-release-architect, engine-product-management, reference-games
- Checks: content creators are first-class; features have an owner through ship; live-ops and patching covered; scale-down keeps small teams productive

### K-FUTURE · Future-Technology Critic

Does the architecture block likely next-5-year technologies: neural rendering, work graphs, cluster RT, ML animation, new storage and memory, new platforms.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1
- Scope: all
- Checks: extension points exist for emerging techniques; maturity labels allow promotion; no hard-coding of today's API limits

### K-COMPLETE · Completeness Critic

Exactly one responsibility: find engine capabilities or engineering disciplines that are missing.

- Stages: G1, G2
- Scope: all
- Checks: compare against shipped engines' feature sets; compare against platform requirements; compare against production pipelines end to end

### K-LEGACY · Anti-Legacy Critic

Find accidental legacy architecture: central sequential update loops, deep inheritance, global state, hot-path virtual dispatch, CPU-driven rendering, coarse locks, global renderer sync, frame-tied lifetimes, universal scene graphs, synchronous IO/loading, single-thread-first design, OpenGL/DX11 assumptions, monoliths. A flagged pattern needs justification, not removal.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: all
- Checks: each pattern in data/legacy-patterns.json absent or justified by an ADR

### K-GAMEPLAY · Game Systems & Content Critic

Animation, audio, AI, gameplay framework, UI, text, localization and accessibility: whether game teams get what they need.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S4, S3
- Scope: subtree:animation-architect, subtree:audio-architect, subtree:gameplay-architect, subtree:ui-architect, accessibility, input-system, input-devices-haptics, character-physics, cinematics-sequencer, systems-simulation, gameplay-camera
- Checks: designers and animators have authoring paths; accessibility and localization built in, not bolted on; gameplay extension points

### K-TEST · Testing & Validation Critic

Validation, oracles, determinism and concurrency testing, agent-output integrity: can an independent critic objectively decide correctness?

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: all, subtree:test-architect, subtree:performance-architect
- Checks: each skill has objective validation with an independent oracle; tests cannot be weakened silently; determinism & concurrency testable via seams; evidence bundle defined for S3/S4

### K-SEC · Security Critic

Threat model, trust boundaries, memory safety, supply chain, privacy, incident response — reviewed at design time as well as in code.

- Stages: G1, G2, S1, S2, S3, S4
- Scope: all, subtree:security-engineering, network-transport, scripting-runtime, modding-ugc, plugin-system, serialization-schema, package-formats-vfs, persistence-save, platform-services, online-services-liveops, packaging-release-patching, ci-cd-automation, build-system-toolchains, observability-telemetry, crash-diagnostics, editor-architect, ai-assisted-authoring, ai-behavior-perception, dedicated-server, asset-import-interchange, privacy-data-protection
- Checks: every untrusted input has a validating owner and a fuzz target; trust boundaries explicit; hardening & key custody; privacy of telemetry, crash and player data
